The bridge is not the failing component. Everything asked for here is now in apw-r85 with the evidence attached.

Fixed. Supervisor.Start and runtime.Run both call srcdsconfig.Install, so both front ends and console mode render server.cfg from the settings that start is using. The redundant call on the Windows start path is gone, and srcdsconfig.RenderServerCfg is extracted so the file can be compared without being written. Recorded, nothing to build. The finding is in the bead and in the comments at both branches of srcdsArgs.

Fixed. MvM_IsGiant now returns false for the sentry buster model, using the same test the defender bot mod already ships in source/redbots3/util.sp. Excluded outright rather than only on self-detonation, which is one rule instead of two. Plugin compiles clean.

Fixed. BUILD_CHANNEL is empty by default so release and local builds are unchanged; nightly.yml passes BUILD_CHANNEL=nightly and the title becomes nightly-<sha>. Verified the Windows -file-version resource stays 1.9.0.0 with the channel set, since goversioninfo needs four numbers.

Fixed. Composition now pads to the team size whenever the blacklist is non-empty, not only when the lineup is empty, so no seat is left for the mod to draw without consulting it. Three new tests cover the short lineup, the no-blacklist case, and a lineup longer than the settings page offers. Two existing expectations changed because they encoded the old behaviour on blacklisted input.

Fixed. The four loops record a retry deadline and the watchdog skips a loop with one booked, plus a one-second grace so it does not race a retry landing on the same poll. A deadline rather than a flag keeps the watchdog's guarantee: a retry that never arrives falls back to it. Chat, deaths and unlocks were fixed alongside grants; they had the same shape and only escaped because nothing held them in the bundle.

Fixed by renaming the asset, which was the recommended option: dist carries env.example with no leading dot, both workflows upload that name, and the two install pages plus their surrounding prose fetch it. Not verified against a live release URL, because GitHub Actions is in a major outage and no release or nightly has completed since the change. The 200/404 check should be redone once one does.

Fixed. Timer_TrimBots is armed after sm_addbots as well as before it, so a poll trims its own overshoot instead of leaving it for a poll that returns early once the wave starts. Bots_TrimSurplus now uses the same seat arithmetic as Bots_Fill via Bots_SeatsHeldOffRed, so RED stops being held full of bots while a reconnecting player sits in spectator. Plugin compiles clean. Not reproduced end to end: the testbed check in the bead (fill to 6, disconnect, reconnect mid-mission) is still worth running.

Fixed. docs/fr/glossary.md is now the same pointer to CONTEXT.md that the English page is, 209 lines down to 15, with a paragraph saying why the terms stay in English. Vale clean on FR rules, make docs-build exit 0.

Fixed for the terminal, which is where the gap was. The Windows window already carried the join addresses on its Session tab; the TUI only had a truncated header list and the C key on the log tab, and the report came from a native Linux player. The session tab now renders ConnectLines: the connect command rather than a bare address, untruncated, with what each reach still needs and the server password when set. No test: the TUI session view needs a running supervisor to render, and ConnectLines has its own tests in internal/runtime. Worth a visual check on a real run.

Documented in both languages, in what-the-randomizer-changes.md under the tickets section. Says logic is per mission and publishes the real REQUIREMENTS table from rules.py: five tiers, not the three MarioSpore had inferred, with the class and slot counts. Vale back to the pre-existing baseline in both files, make docs-build exit 0.

Fixed, and the bead's guess was wrong: not a client that missed the datapackage, but the bridge never asking for one. printJSON.text read only the Text field, which carries the id itself for typed parts. The bridge now sends GetDataPackage on connect for the games in the room, keeps names per game because two games may both number an item 77, and takes player names free from Connected. Five tests cover resolution, the game-picking, unresolved and ambiguous ids, and the pre-handshake case. Not seen against a live room: worth one look at chat on the next run.

Fixed. /missions serves played alongside cleared, and the GUI and TUI both draw them apart: 'cleared' means this server played it, 'collected' means only the room holds the check. Cleared keeps its old meaning because the plugin chains on it. Test covers the disagreement directly. Not seen against a live room with another world collecting.

ItemServerLine matches the 'Current item schema is up-to-date' success line, verified against two real bundles, and passes anything else about the schema through without interpreting it. The GUI prints it; the TUI keeps it on the session tab so it does not scroll away. Whether the fetch itself belongs here or on the mod side is still unresolved and out of scope for the message.

Exercised against a stub docker in both directions: recovers when the third attempt succeeds, and still exits 1 with 'push failed 3 times' when every attempt fails. cancel-in-progress deliberately left alone.

Fixed. botTeamEditor.refreshLoadouts refills every seat and class loadout
menu, and the Loadouts page calls it after Save and after Remove.

The selection is put back by name rather than by index, because saving a
loadout inserts it among the others and every index after it moves; and by name
rather than by the whole label, because saving over a name changes the weapons
the label spells out and the menu should stay on the loadout the seat still
names. A removed loadout falls back to index zero, which is the class's stock.

reselectLoadout carries that rule and lives in the non-Windows file, so three
tests cover it: one asserts the new loadout really did shift the picked index
before checking the pick survived, or it would prove nothing.

Also fixed while here: botTeamEditor.show resolved a saved team's loadouts with
class.LoadoutByKey, which knows nothing about custom ones, so loading a team
that named a custom loadout showed stock. It goes through the library now.

All three done, in the GUI and the TUI where each applies.

The tab is 'Networking' in both interfaces and in the TUI's tab test. Both

Fixed, and the cause was one line: botlive.seatAt asked class.LoadoutByKey,
which only knows the presets this package ships, so every custom key resolved

Two tests, and both print 'Stock weapons' without the fix: one for a loadout on

One fix covers all three surfaces, since the GUI tab, the TUI tab and !ap bots

The same mistake was in the settings window's team Load and went with apw-5nv

WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu no longer displays an empty menu: it returns false and frees the Menu when nothing was listed, and the disabled 'No buffs for this loadout yet' item is gone. Command_WeaponBuffs answers in chat on false. The MvM_UpgradesBegin path in MvM_OnCommandKeyValues now draws nothing and takes no number keys when the loadout has no buff.

Not a code fix: the heal is accepted and written down at MvM_PackCredits. Only Scouts are healed by a credit pile, per pile rather than per credit, 50 below full and 25 as overheal at full. Bundles pay between waves with everybody at full health at the upgrade station, so the real case is 25 decaying overheal on one class, and nothing at all on the servers where item_currencypack_custom carries no amount property and the m_nCurrency fallback pays instead. Too small to trade against the accounting hole that produced apw-6hf, and too small for a health read-back.

Kept on purpose, decided with the numbers in hand.

The heal is Scouts only, 25 points of decaying overheal per pile between waves,
and the same whether the bundle is worth 50 credits or 1000. On servers where
item_currencypack_custom carries no amount property the pack path never runs at
all and the fallback heals nothing.

All three fixes cost more than that. Reordering the payment paths pushes every
bundle through g_BundleCredits and widens the surface that produced apw-6hf.
Suppressing the heal has no hook, since the pickup is the payment. Subtracting
the healed amount reads health across a frame boundary against overheal the game
is already decaying.

Recorded in the doc block above MvM_PackCredits so the next reader does not file
this again. Reopen if a Scout-heavy team ever makes 25 points matter.

Fixed in defenderbots v2.21.2 and verified.

Two faults, both mod side. BluAssist_OnRobotSpawn ran inside the player_spawn
frame, where the popfile is still building the robot and overwrote it; it now
defers a frame. And a raw m_iMaxHealth write does not stick because TF2
recomputes the maximum from attributes, so health goes through 'max health
additive bonus' as a delta. Speed was also replacing the template's move speed
bonus instead of multiplying it.

Fixed. guard wraps the bridge, the game server, the SourceMod error watcher and
the supervisor, which are the four goroutines that outlive the call starting
them.

Not a swallow: the panic and its stack go to the log a debug bundle carries,
which is louder than the silent exit it replaces.

Two tests. The first caught a real mistake in itself rather than in the code: it
signalled from inside the guarded work, whose defers run while the panic is
still unwinding, so it read the result before recover had written it. Race
detector and lint clean.

Also audited in the same pass and found clean: the plugin's natives. Every
GetEntProp goes through HasProp and every RequestFrame callback through
MvM_IsPlayer, which checks IsClientInGame. That is the crash class the bots repo
had, in mvm-ijg, and this repo does not.
